keywords.def: saying no to someone; refusing an idea or suggestion
worried about speaking to other people, or being judged when around others
feeling that everything you do needs to be perfect

sentences.en: Hello and welcome to 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Georgie. And I'm Neil. Don't forget you can find vocabulary, definitions and a worksheet for free on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我是 Georgie。我是 Neil。别忘了，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 免费获取词汇表、释义和练习题。

sentences.en: So Neil, today we're talking about rejection.
sentences.zh: Neil，我们今天要聊的是“拒绝”（rejection）。

sentences.en: So, rejection means saying no to someone or refusing to accept their idea or suggestion.
sentences.zh: “Rejection”的意思是对某人说“不”，或者拒绝接受他们的想法或提议。

sentences.en: Neil, how do you feel about rejection? Well, nobody likes rejection.
sentences.zh: Neil，你对被拒绝有什么感觉？嗯，没人喜欢被拒绝。

sentences.en: But I think as you get older, you get used to it.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得随着年龄的增长，你会对此习以为常。

sentences.en: And probably it's quite a good thing to experience rejection, even if it doesn't feel nice.
sentences.zh: 而且，即便体验拒绝的感觉并不好受，但这可能也是件挺好的事。

sentences.en: Yeah, I agree. We can't always get what we want, can we?
sentences.zh: 是啊，我同意。我们不可能总是心想事成，对吧？

sentences.en: We can't, no. In this podcast, we'll be learning about a new internet trend called rejection therapy and how people are using it to help them to be more confident.
sentences.zh: 确实不能。在本期播客中，我们将了解一种被称为“拒绝疗法”（rejection therapy）的网络新趋势，以及人们是如何利用它来帮助自己建立自信的。

sentences.en: OK. Let's start with our quiz question, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 好的。Georgie，我们先从今天的测验题开始吧。

sentences.en: Lots of famous people have faced rejection in their lives before they became successful, but which of these things did not happen to the animator Walt Disney before he became successful?
sentences.zh: 许多名人在成功前都曾经历过拒绝，但在动画大师 Walt Disney 成功之前，下列哪件事并没有发生在他身上？

sentences.en: Was it: a) he lost his job as an artist, b) his first business ran out of money, or c) his first full length film was a failure?
sentences.zh: 选项是：a) 他失去了画师的工作，b) 他的第一家公司资金耗尽，还是 c) 他的第一部长篇电影失败了？

sentences.en: I've got no idea, but I'm going to go with a) he lost his job as an artist.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道，但我选 a) 他失去了画师的工作。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的。节目最后我们再来揭晓答案。

sentences.en: OK Neil. So, most people don't like being rejected, but one thing to try might be something called rejection therapy.
sentences.zh: 好的，Neil。大多数人都不喜欢被拒绝，但有一种可以尝试的方法，叫做“拒绝疗法”。

sentences.en: It's a social media trend where people record themselves talking to strangers and sometimes being rejected.
sentences.zh: 这是一种社交媒体潮流，人们会录下自己与陌生人搭话，有时还会被拒绝的过程。

sentences.en: OK. That sounds quite interesting, but let's find out how it works in practice.
sentences.zh: 好的。听起来挺有意思的，那我们来看看它在实践中是如何运作的吧。

sentences.en: Hannah Gelbart, host of the BBC World Service podcast What in the World, had a go at the trend.
sentences.zh: BBC World Service 播客《What in the World》的主持人 Hannah Gelbart 亲身体验了这一潮流。

sentences.en: Let's see how she got on. Hey, can I come sit down at your table?
sentences.zh: 我们来看看她进展如何。嘿，我可以坐你们这桌吗？

sentences.en: Yeah. Hey, how's it going? Good, thank you.
sentences.zh: 可以啊。嗨，最近怎么样？挺好的，谢谢。

sentences.en: How's your day gone? Good afternoon. How are you doing?
sentences.zh: 今天过得怎么样？下午好。你最近好吗？

sentences.en: Can I drive your cab?
sentences.zh: 我能开一下你的出租车吗？

sentences.en: Can I? Can I get behind the wheel? Don't be silly!
sentences.zh: 可以吗？我能去坐驾驶位吗？别闹了！

sentences.en: Don't be silly...! Coming somewhere else to try and face my fears... maybe do a bit of shopping.
sentences.zh: 别开玩笑了……！换个地方继续直面我的恐惧……顺便逛逛街。

sentences.en: I was wondering, can I have a nap in one of these beds?
sentences.zh: 我想问一下，我能在这些床上睡个午觉吗？

sentences.en: Can I just try it out? Wow – I didn't expect that one to be a yes!
sentences.zh: 我能试躺一下吗？哇——真没想到这次对方居然答应了！

sentences.en: Well, it seems like people were pretty nice to Hannah in those examples.
sentences.zh: 嗯，看来在这些例子里，大家对 Hannah 还挺友善的。

sentences.en: Yes. And she talks with psychologist Claudia Hammond about how she felt during the experiment.
sentences.zh: 是的。她还和心理学家 Claudia Hammond 探讨了自己在实验过程中的感受。

sentences.en: And actually, walking up to the first person, I felt my adrenaline really, really spiking.
sentences.zh: 其实在走向第一个人时，我感觉自己的肾上腺素真的在疯狂飙升。

sentences.en: I'm not a socially anxious person – I think I'm really confident.
sentences.zh: 我不是个有社交焦虑的人——我认为自己其实很自信。

sentences.en: But that first thing really scared me. And once I'd done one, the second one came easier and the third one came even easier.
sentences.zh: 但那第一次尝试真的吓到我了。而一旦做完第一次，第二次就变得容易了，第三次就更容易了。

sentences.en: And you know, by the fourth time I didn't even mind it whether they said yes or no.
sentences.zh: 到了第四次，不管对方说好还是说不，我其实都已经不在意了。

sentences.en: Hannah says that when she walked up to the first stranger in the video, she felt her adrenaline spiking.
sentences.zh: Hannah 说，当她在视频中走向第一个陌生人时，她感到肾上腺素飙升（spiking）。

sentences.en: If something spikes, it increases sharply.
sentences.zh: 如果某样东西“spikes”，意思是它急剧上升。

sentences.en: Hannah is not generally a socially anxious person.
sentences.zh: Hannah 通常并不是一个有社交焦虑（socially anxious）的人。

sentences.en: Someone who is socially anxious is nervous or worried about speaking to other people.
sentences.zh: 有社交焦虑的人在与他人交谈时会感到紧张或担忧。

sentences.en: Each time Hannah tried to speak to a new person, she says, it came easier.
sentences.zh: Hannah 说，每次尝试与新人交谈，事情都会变得更容易（came easier）。

sentences.en: Come easier is an informal way to say something is easier to achieve.
sentences.zh: “Come easier”是一种非正式表达，意思是一件事变得更容易做到了。

sentences.en: Now, this social media trend is called rejection therapy, but it's not a proper form of therapy.
sentences.zh: 虽然这种社交媒体潮流被称为“拒绝疗法”，但它并不是一种正式的治疗手段。

sentences.en: It hasn't been tested. And there are some criticisms of the videos because they involve filming your interactions with strangers, which people might not want.
sentences.zh: 它尚未经过科学验证。而且这些视频也受到了一些批评，因为拍摄涉及与陌生人的互动，而对方可能并不希望被拍。

sentences.en: But people who post the videos say they boost their confidence.
sentences.zh: 但发布视频的人表示，这确实增强了他们的自信心。

sentences.en: So, why do people want to ask for rejection?
sentences.zh: 那么，人们为什么会主动去“求拒绝”呢？

sentences.en: Psychologist Claudia Hammond has some ideas, which she shared with Hannah on the BBC World Service podcast What in the World.
sentences.zh: 心理学家 Claudia Hammond 有一些看法，她在 BBC World Service 的播客《What in the World》中与 Hannah 分享了这些观点。

sentences.en: What we do know is that there is an increase in perfectionism.
sentences.zh: 我们确知的是，完美主义倾向（perfectionism）正在抬头。

sentences.en: People are more worried now, younger people, about how other people are judging them.
sentences.zh: 现在的年轻人更加担心别人会怎样评判自己。

sentences.en: And so, I wonder whether that might make people more shy of speaking to strangers – worried that the people will, you know, not appraise them in a good way, and so doing something like this to try to counter that might feel like a positive step to people, that they're trying to do something.
sentences.zh: 所以我在想，这是否会让大家更羞于与陌生人交谈——担心别人对自己的评价不高。因此，通过做这样的事情来对抗这种心理，大家可能会觉得是一种积极的尝试，至少说明他们在做出努力。

sentences.en: Also, they're fun to watch. Claudia says there's an increase in perfectionism among young people.
sentences.zh: 而且，这些视频看起也挺有意思的。Claudia 表示，年轻群体中的完美主义倾向正在上升。

sentences.en: Perfectionism is the feeling that everything you do needs to be perfect.
sentences.zh: 完美主义（perfectionism）是指觉得凡事都必须做到尽善尽美的一种心态。

sentences.en: Young people are also worried about how people will appraise them, which means judge them.
sentences.zh: 年轻人还担心别人会如何评估（appraise）他们，也就是评判他们。

sentences.en: Deliberately looking for rejection might be an extreme way to become more confident, but it can lead to surprising discoveries.
sentences.zh: 故意寻求拒绝也许是建立自信的一种极端方式，但它可能会带来令人惊喜的发现。

sentences.en: Yes, and Hannah found that most strangers she spoke to were friendly and happy to help, so she didn't really experience rejection much at all.
sentences.zh: 是的，Hannah 发现与她交谈的大多数陌生人都很友善且乐于助人，所以她实际上并没有经历多少次拒绝。

sentences.en: OK. Georgie, I think it's time now for the answer to my quiz question.
sentences.zh: 好的。Georgie，我想现在是揭晓测验题答案的时候了。

sentences.en: I asked you which rejection Walt Disney didn't experience before becoming successful?
sentences.zh: 我刚才问你，Walt Disney 在成功之前并没有经历过哪种挫折？

sentences.en: Yes, and I went for a) I don't think he lost his job as an artist.
sentences.zh: 是的，我选了 a)，我认为他没有失去画师的工作。

sentences.en: Well, actually, the answer was c) his first full length film, Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, was not a failure.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实答案是 c)：他的第一部长篇电影《白雪公主与七个小矮人》并没有失败。

sentences.en: It was a huge success. Wow! That was his first film?
sentences.zh: 它取得了巨大的成功。哇！那是他的第一部电影吗？

sentences.en: That's really impressive. It is. OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with rejection, which means saying no or refusing an idea or suggestion.
sentences.zh: 那真是太厉害了。确实是。好了，我们来回顾一下本期节目中学到的词汇吧，首先是“rejection”，意思是对某人说不，或拒绝某种想法或提议。

sentences.en: The verb spike means increase suddenly. Someone who is socially anxious is nervous or worried about speaking to other people.
sentences.zh: 动词“spike”意思是猛增、急剧上升。有社交焦虑（socially anxious）的人在与他人交谈时会感到紧张或担忧。

sentences.en: If something comes easier, it's easier to achieve.
sentences.zh: 如果某事变得“comes easier”，意思就是它更容易达成了。

sentences.en: Perfectionism is the feeling that everything you do needs to be perfect.
sentences.zh: 完美主义（perfectionism）是指认为自己所做的一切都必须完美的想法。

sentences.en: And if you appraise someone, you judge them.
sentences.zh: 如果你去“appraise”某人，意思就是你对他们做出评估或评判。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but you can test what you've learned with the free worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了，但你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上使用免费练习题来检验你的学习成果。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us and goodbye. Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 感谢你的收听，再见。再见。
